# Inaras: the stories first, then the spelling

You cannot weigh an accent without knowing what it carries. Here is what **Inaras** has been carrying.

## The Stories That Carry the Name

**The Feast of the Dragon.** After the storm-god Tarḫunash is defeated by the dragon Illuyanka, Inaras takes action.  She prepares an enormous feast of beer, wine, and every kind of food, then goes to the mortal Ḫupašiya and proposes a bargain: if he helps her trap the dragon, she will sleep with him.  Ḫupašiya agrees.

**Inaras and Ḫupašiya.** The myth places a mortal at the center of divine victory.  Inaras does not defeat the dragon alone; she enlists human cunning and desire.  After the deed she warns Ḫupašiya not to look out the window while she is away, but he disobeys and sees his family.

**Lady of the Steppe.** As goddess of the wild animals, Inaras guarantees the abundance of game and the balance between human hunters and animal herds.  Her domain is the dangerous, fertile margin between the settled land of Hatti and the wilderness beyond.

## The Name Travels

Inaras shares traits with several ancient Mediterranean and Near Eastern figures. Her role as mistress of animals recalls the Greek Potnia Theron, the Mistress of Animals who presides over wild creatures, and Artemis in her capacity as huntress.

## The Address It Earned

The temple of **Inaras** stands at [/inaras/](/inaras/) — [lore](/inaras/lore/), [scholars](/inaras/scholars/), [patterns](/inaras/patterns/) — because a name carrying this much story deserves more than a parking page. Tier-2 here means one preserved truth — not less important, just singular. The temple shows it and names it.

## The Emblems

The name does not travel alone. **Gazelle** — The swift animal of the steppe, emblem of her wild domain.; **Bow and arrow** — The tools of the hunt and the means by which she governs animals.; **Feast** — The banquet of beer and wine by which Illuyanka is lulled and trapped.. Each emblem is filed in the temple's record with its own provenance, the same discipline the spelling gets.

## For the Voice

Scholarly reconstruction /iˈnaːras/; the exact ancient pronunciation is debated. The reconstructed line runs `/iˈnaːras/` — the temple's pronunciation atlas carries the phonemes one by one.
